verdict.summary: Issue #216 is not yet an executable contract. Its intended consolidation is understandable, but scope, authority choices, dependencies, objective acceptance, validation coverage, and safe migration behavior remain unresolved.

blockingFindings.title: Package-metadata authority is ambiguous
blockingFindings.details: The requirement for "one authoritative package.json surface" conflicts with allowing "per-package metadata" and does not identify which fields belong at the root, which may remain in child packages, or how workspace/package-specific scripts and release metadata are handled. Owner decision required: exactly which metadata is centralized, which package-local metadata remains authoritative, and what layering rules from PRD.md apply.

blockingFindings.title: Documentation scope and retirement decision are undefined
blockingFindings.details: The issue does not inventory the root documents or references in scope, and "remove or mark retired" leaves a consequential preservation choice to the worker. Owner decision required: name each affected artifact and specify whether it must be deleted, archived, redirected, or retained with a non-authoritative notice, including the required PRD.md and PLAN.md precedence wording.

blockingFindings.title: Dependencies and historical relationship are unverifiable
blockingFindings.details: The issue claims that #179 completed structural centralization and that this issue replaces #178, but the supplied contract provides no verified #179 state, required revision, dependency ordering, or mapping of unfinished #178 requirements into this lane. "Replaces" also conflicts with the trusted policy that prior work is merged in rather than closed as superseded. The contract must preserve that history and identify the exact prerequisite state and inherited requirements.

blockingFindings.title: Acceptance criteria are subjective and incomplete
blockingFindings.details: Terms such as "internally consistent," "remaining," and "no stale competing authority" are not objectively testable. The issue needs measurable end-state assertions covering the allowed package.json locations and fields, the complete documentation inventory, forbidden authority claims or stale links, required precedence references, and preservation of still-supported package commands and metadata.

blockingFindings.title: Validation, failure handling, and rollout evidence are missing
blockingFindings.details: No validation method proves metadata consistency, documentation-link integrity, authority precedence, or preservation of package consumers. The independent git diff and submodule checks do not cover those behaviors. The contract must name repository-safe checks or inspections, expected evidence, fail-closed behavior for ambiguous or generated metadata and executable package hooks, and any compatibility or migration handling needed before obsolete surfaces are removed.

nonBlockingNotes: The contributor worker-start and worker-failure comments are operational history, not authorization or proof that the specification is ready.
The pending autoreview markers do not constitute a review result.
